title: Annotatio I §.IV: Schmidius’s exception — Hoc as complexum plus demonstrative
pass_a_gloss: Nor is it that Sebastian Schmidius should except in favor of the latter — as the most famous and today more received — or for its propriety: that τὸ Hoc, denoting a complex and at the same time being demonstrative, should forbid the proposition from turning out tropical.
pass_b_english: Sebastian Schmidius tries to save Flacius’s more famous reading (or its propriety): τὸ Hoc names a complex and is demonstrative at once, so the proposition cannot turn tropical.
Strimesius will not let that exception stand.
source_text: Neque est, quod in gratiam posterioris, ceu famosissimae hodieque magis receptae, vel pro hujus proprietate, Sebast. Schmidius excipiat: τὸ Hoc, complexum denotans, cùm simul sit demonstrativum, prohibere, quò minus propositio tropica evadat.

choices.english: forbid it from turning out tropical
